names.official: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe

summary: São Tomé and Príncipe exempts citizens of the EU, the US, Canada and the member countries of the Portuguese-speaking CPLP from visas under Law 5/2015, and the UK and US governments say their citizens can visit without a visa for up to 15 days, Canada's for stays of less than 15 days. The law also exempts nationals of countries covered by visa-abolition or free-movement agreements, and for up to fifteen days nationals of third countries set by Government decree; no official source we could read lists those countries. Otherwise, Law 5/2008 requires foreigners to hold a valid entry visa to enter. The Migration and Border Service says someone living abroad where there is no São Toméan consulate cannot get a visa on arrival at the border and needs an entry authorisation (AE), requested through its eVisaST portal and presented on arrival.

tips.text: The UK and US governments say their citizens can visit without a visa for up to 15 days, and Canada's says for stays of less than 15 days. Under Law 5/2008 a longer stay can be granted as an extension, which is for the director of the Migration and Border Service to grant.

The US State Department says São Tomé and Príncipe has a cash-based economy and advises carrying only large US dollar notes ($100 bills), as small bills are not accepted at banks or exchange offices; Canada says US dollars, euros and CFA francs are widely accepted for exchange at banks.
Canada's travel advice lists malaria among the diseases travellers to São Tomé and Príncipe might be at risk for that can be prevented with vaccines or medications.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for São Tomé and Príncipe?
faq.answer: Citizens of the EU, the US, Canada and the member countries of the Portuguese-speaking CPLP are exempt from visas under Law 5/2015. The UK government says British visitors can visit for tourism without a visa for up to 15 days, the US government says the same 15 days for its citizens and Canada's says Canadians need no tourist visa for stays of less than 15 days. The law also exempts nationals of countries covered by visa-abolition or free-movement agreements, and for up to fifteen days nationals of third countries set by Government decree; no official source we could read lists those countries. Otherwise, Law 5/2008 requires foreigners to hold a valid entry visa to enter. The Migration and Border Service (SMF) says someone living abroad where there is no São Toméan consulate cannot get a visa on arrival at the border and needs an entry authorisation (AE), requested through its eVisaST portal and presented on arrival.

faq.question: How can I stay longer than 15 days?
faq.answer: Under Law 5/2008 (articles 42 to 44), a foreigner admitted with or without a visa who wants to stay longer than allowed on entry can have the stay extended; for those admitted without a visa the extension is up to thirty days, extendable for an equal period, and granting it is the exclusive competence of the director of the Migration and Border Service.

faq.question: Is yellow fever vaccination required for São Tomé and Príncipe?
faq.answer: The UK government says you need a yellow fever certificate if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk.

faq.question: What money should I bring to São Tomé and Príncipe?
faq.answer: The US State Department says São Tomé and Príncipe has a cash-based economy, that international credit cards (Visa only) can be used at ATMs and some large stores and restaurants, and that main hotels accept other international cards; it advises carrying only large US dollar notes ($100 bills), as small bills are not accepted at banks or exchange offices. Canada says US dollars, euros and Central African CFA francs are widely accepted for exchange at banks.
